summary: WP-001 passes code review. Implementation is minimal, correct, and non-breaking. One Fix-Forward applied: added XML constructor documentation covering parameter semantics, thread affinity of the callback, and the edge-case behaviour when onComplete itself throws (exception caught by existing catch(Exception ex) handler, surfacing as an error state rather than escaping unhandled — contrary to QA's note). All four AC remain met. Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings after edit.

comments.note: ProvisioningToolsViewModel.cs constructor: Added full XML documentation comment (summary + provisioner param + onComplete param). Documents that (1) the callback fires once on success, never on cancel/throw; (2) it executes on a ThreadPool thread due to ConfigureAwait(false) — callers must self-dispatch to the UI thread if needed; (3) if the callback throws, its exception is caught by the catch(Exception ex) handler and surfaced via Error, placing the VM in a failed state even though provisioning itself succeeded. Non-behavioral change; QA validation remains intact.

QA handoff note stated the onComplete exception 'escapes RunProvisioningAsync unhandled'. This is inaccurate: the exception is caught by the existing catch(Exception ex) block and written to Error. The real concern is that a throwing callback masks a successful provisioning run with an error state. The new XML doc captures the correct semantics.

Overall: implementation is clean, idiomatic, and well-scoped. The readonly Action? field, optional constructor parameter, and null-conditional invoke pattern are all best-practice C# for this kind of callback extension. No architectural concerns.
